sources.title: Manolis Kellis, 6.096 Algorithms for Computational Biology, Lecture 7: Gene Finding and HMMs, MIT OpenCourseWare (Spring 2005)
sources.locator: PDF pp. 6–7 for the finite HMM parameterization and decoding objective; pp. 20–25 for the dynamic-programming derivation, max-product recurrence, backpointers, complexity, and log-domain underflow discussion.
sources.source_kind_detail: Complete 69-page MIT OpenCourseWare lecture PDF. The full document was downloaded and text-extracted; the cited HMM and decoding pages were inspected in full, including the recurrence derivation and traceback instructions.

read_evidence.extent: The complete PDF was fetched and text-extracted with MuPDF. The HMM definition, path-probability factorization, sequence-decoding objective, recurrence derivation, initialization, termination, traceback, complexity, underflow note, and posterior-decoding distinction on the cited pages were inspected. The local claims use exact finite products and supply complete proofs; no source formula replaces a local proof.

contents.name: HMM finite state, observation, initial, transition, and emission data; path probability
contents.detail: The local definition fixes finite discrete sets, row-normalized parameters, the exact joint path mass, observation evidence, and the positive-evidence condition for a posterior.

contents.name: The sequence-decoding objective and its max-product dynamic-programming recurrence
contents.detail: The source recurrence is specialized from HMMs to the local finite weighted trellis, with an explicit no-positive-path branch and complete predecessor traceback.

contents.name: The Viterbi recurrence, traceback, and finite operation count
contents.detail: The local proof derives the prefix recurrence by finite path decomposition and proves the returned path maximizes the full trellis score.

contents.name: Posterior decoding and sequence decoding are distinct; coordinatewise modes need not form a best path
contents.detail: The source warns that posterior decoding may yield an invalid state sequence. The local example gives a normalized two-state model where the unique coordinatewise modes form a strictly suboptimal sequence.

contents.name: Log-domain implementation to reduce floating-point underflow
contents.reason: This batch states exact real-valued max-product recurrences and makes no floating-point stability or log-domain implementation claim.

sources.title: Stanford CS262, Lecture 7: Hidden Markov Models

sources.source_kind_detail: Complete 26-page Stanford CS262 lecture PDF. The full document was downloaded and text-extracted; the cited model and single-sequence decoding pages were inspected in full.

read_evidence.extent: The complete PDF was fetched and text-extracted with MuPDF. The HMM parameter list, single-sequence Viterbi state score, transition/emission recurrence, and pair-HMM extension on the cited pages were inspected. The pair-HMM material is explicitly excluded; local claims retain only the single-sequence finite-state interface and prove their own exactness.

contents.name: Finite HMM parameterization and the single-sequence Viterbi objective
contents.detail: The local definition states the same finite-state ingredients while fixing the joint-law normalization and zero-evidence conventions explicitly.

contents.name: Single-sequence max-product recurrence and termination
contents.detail: The local construction embeds the observed HMM in a layered weighted trellis and invokes the previously defined finite-trellis Viterbi procedure.

contents.name: Pair-HMM sequence alignment recurrences
contents.reason: Pair-HMMs and sequence alignment are outside the assigned single-sequence HMM and finite-trellis scope.

pages.source_context: The companion examples use the two independently inspected full-text lecture treatments recorded for the A page; every finite score and probability is also verified directly from its explicit local model.

supported_examples.detail: All admissible paths, scores, unreachable-state recurrence values, and tie-breaking output are computed from the displayed finite trellis.
All eight hidden paths, the evidence probability, the max-product table, and traceback are computed exactly as rational numbers.
Both hidden paths have zero joint mass for the observed symbol, so evidence is zero and conditional sequence probabilities are undefined.
The finite joint path masses, both one-time marginals, and the strict comparison between the coordinatewise mode and sequence MAP are computed exactly.
